Cover illustration for a lifehacker.dev Hacks article.

TITLE — typeset this exact headline, large, high-contrast, in the vertical middle 60% of the frame. No other words, no byline, no watermark, no logo:
Auto-deploy a Jekyll site over FTP from CI (the Travis recipe, legacy but real)

SUBJECT
Build Jekyll in CI and FTP _site to a host that only speaks FTP via ncftp. The real .travis.yml, the deploy script, and the rm -rf window that downs your site.

NOTES
Some hosting plans give you exactly one way in: FTP. No SSH, no rsync, no git push, no S3. One username, one password, and a folder called that your website lives in. Meanwhile your source sits on GitHub and you would like, very much, to stop dragging files into FileZilla by hand every time you fix a typo. This is the bridge: CI builds the Jekyll site on every push, then a deploy script FTPs the compiled up to the host. The original recipe here used Travis CI, and Travis CI for open source repos

ART DIRECTION
Trace Bloom: dark field #05070d over #0b1020, lattice #1b2b44, signal #22d3ee, heat #f472b6, ink #eaf6ff, accent #22d3ee. Diagrammatic, high-contrast, cinematic 3:2 landscape. Draw the concrete apparatus this article is about — not a generic circuit board, robot, brain, or rocket. No faces. No UI chrome. No stock-tech collage. The still frame must read at 300px.
